Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What failed: In DOMModelTest.testAxisAttribute(), the last assertion evaluates the XPath vendor/product/price:amount/attribute::node() and expects all attributes of the element, returning the set {"10%", "20%"}.
- How the expression is parsed: attribute::node() compiles to an attribute-axis step with a NodeTypeTest for node() (i.e., “match any node” on the attribute axis).
- How it’s evaluated: AttributeContext drives evaluation of the attribute axis. In AttributeContext.nextNode(), the code currently does:
  - On first call, it checks if nodeTest is an instance of NodeNameTest.
  - If not, it immediately returns false without creating an iterator:
    - if (!(nodeTest instanceof NodeNameTest)) { return false; }
  - When the check passes, it creates an attribute iterator using the provided QName.
- Why this breaks: For attribute::node(), nodeTest is a NodeTypeTest (not a NodeNameTest). Because AttributeContext only accepts NodeNameTest, it returns false, never creating a DOMAttributeIterator, and yields no attributes. Hence, the test that expects two attribute nodes fails.
- What should happen: node() on the attribute axis should match all attributes of the current element. The DOM layer already supports this: DOMAttributeIterator, when constructed with a QName whose local name is "*", iterates all attributes and filters out xmlns declarations. Therefore, AttributeContext only needs to map attribute::node() to a wildcard QName and iterate.
- Supporting evidence:
  - AttributeContext.nextNode() at lines 75–81 rejects any NodeTest that is not NodeNameTest and thus cannot handle node().
  - DOMAttributeIterator handles wildcards by iterating all attributes when name.getName().equals("*"), and testAttr() filters namespace declarations appropriately.
  - The current bug report proposes exactly this: introducing a wildcard QName ("*") and using it when the test is not a NodeNameTest (i.e., for node()).

Root cause:
AttributeContext.nextNode() is overly restrictive; it only supports NodeNameTest and rejects NodeTypeTest for node(), causing attribute::node() to return an empty sequence instead of all attributes. The fix is to treat node() on the attribute axis as a wildcard by passing a QName("*") to the attribute iterator (and possibly handling other legal cases similarly).
